name: Korean Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Semantic Scholar API search 'Korean Sign Language prosody' (receipt)
sources.note: Only prosody hit for KSL is Lee & Choi 2025; other hits are sign recognition engineering, toponyms, pedagogy.

sources.citation: Lee, Jungah & Youngju Choi. 2025. Visual prosody in Korean Sign Language: (non)manual cues for boundary and prominence. Frontiers in Psychology 16:1601842. doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2025.1601842
sources.note: Nothing on word-level/lexical stress. Studies phrase-level prominence (focus) vs AP-boundary marking; concludes KSL prosody is 'prominence-driven', marked mainly by nonmanuals (eye contact, furrowed eyebrows, squinted eyes) and sign duration; states (p.6 fn.5) 'Prior research on KSL prosody is extremely limited' and that NIKL (2021) only notes pauses and final-sign lengthening at phrase boundaries.

sources.note: Contains the KSL chapter (Nam & Byun) and possibly phonology chapters on East Asian sign languages; could confirm absence/presence of any lexical prominence description for KSL.

sources.citation: National Institute of Korean Language (국립국어원). 2021. 한국수어 문법 [Korean Sign Language grammar]. Seoul: NIKL.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The official KSL grammar; the only work Lee & Choi cite for KSL prosody (pauses, final lengthening). If any first-hand statement on sign-internal prominence/rhythm exists it would be here (in Korean). NIKL publications are usually free PDFs on korean.go.
